items.stem: You need the total sales per customer repeated on every row regardless of other dimensions in the view. Which calculation type fits?

options.rationale: Correct: a FIXED LOD computes at a defined granularity independent of the view's dimensions.
A table calculation depends on the layout of the view, not a fixed granularity.
A row-level calculation evaluates per data row, not aggregated per customer.
A parameter is a single user-controlled value, not a per-customer aggregate.

items.stem: Which Tableau feature lets a selection in one chart filter another chart on the same dashboard?

options.rationale: Correct: a filter action passes a selection from one sheet to filter others.
A calculated field creates new values, not interactivity between charts.
A data blend combines data sources; it does not drive dashboard interactivity.
A trend line is an analytic overlay, not an interaction.

items.explanation: Correct: a filter action passes a selection from one sheet to filter others.

items.stem: Which TWO practices help a published Tableau dashboard perform well on a large data source? (Select TWO)

options.text: Use an extract instead of a live connection where freshness allows
options.rationale: Correct: extracts are optimized columnar snapshots that usually query faster than live connections.

options.text: Reduce the number of marks and high-cardinality quick filters
options.rationale: Correct: fewer marks and filters reduce rendering and query load.

options.text: Add as many worksheets as possible to one dashboard
options.rationale: More worksheets increase queries and rendering cost, hurting performance.

options.text: Replace all aggregates with row-level detail
options.rationale: Row-level detail returns far more data and typically slows the dashboard.
